introduction: On this Sunday, Genesis tells how God created man and woman to be one flesh. In the Gospel, Jesus teaches about the permanence of marriage, then welcomes the little children and blesses them. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Jesus is not ashamed to call us his brothers and sisters. Let us pray for married couples and families, and receive God's Kingdom like little children.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, blessed are those who fear the Lord and walk in his ways. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For married couples: that they may grow in faithful love, and that God may strengthen those who are struggling. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose marriages have broken down, and for their children: that they may find healing and the support of the Church. Let us pray to the Lord.
For engaged couples preparing for marriage: that they may build their life together on God's love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For children everywhere: that they may be welcomed, loved and blessed. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may receive the Kingdom of God with the trust of little children. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you created man and woman for one another and blessed their union. Strengthen husbands and wives in faithful love, and bless our families. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: No longer two, but one
reflection.body:
The second chapter of Genesis tells a story about loneliness and love. God sees that "It is not good for the man to be alone." None of the animals is a fitting partner. So God forms the woman and brings her to the man, and he cries out with joy: "This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh." Then comes the sentence that describes marriage: "Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh."

In the Gospel, the Pharisees ask Jesus whether divorce is permitted. He takes them back to that beginning: "from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female." He quotes Genesis and adds, "so that they are no longer two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate." Jesus restores God's original plan for marriage as a lifelong covenant.

This teaching is demanding, and many people carry the pain of broken marriages. The Church holds firmly to the words of Jesus, and she is also called to accompany with compassion those who suffer, and their children.

Right after this teaching, people bring children to Jesus, and the disciples try to send them away. Jesus is indignant: "Allow the little children to come to me! Don't forbid them, for God's Kingdom belongs to such as these." He takes them in his arms and blesses them.

The Letter to the Hebrews reminds us that Jesus shared our human life, and "he is not ashamed to call them brothers." This week, pray for the married couples you know, especially any who are struggling. If you are married, thank God for your spouse and tell them so. And bring your own family to Jesus to be blessed.
